newsitem.title: USA: Bail for teenagers in Delaware baby murder case.
newsitem.headline: Bail for teenagers in Delaware baby murder case.

text.p: A Delaware judge on Tuesday set bail of $300,000 each for two New Jersey teenagers indicted on first-degree murder charges in the death of their new-born son last year.
In a one-hour hearing in Superior Court, Judge Henry DuPont Ridgely ordered 18-year-olds Amy Grossberg and Brian Peterson, from Bergen County, to be released on bail under strict conditions.
Although bail is unusual in capital crime cases, the Delaware attorney general withdrew objections last week, saying the two posed no threat to the public.
According to deputy attorney general Peter Letang, the state still intends to seek the death penalty at a trial scheduled to begin on Sept. 9.

In addition to the bail, which is expected to be posted by their parents, the college students will be required to live at home, be monitored electronically, give up their passports, and waive domestic and international extradition. They will also have to observe an 8 p.m.-to-6 a.m. curfew, and be in regular contact with officials of the Delaware Corrections Department.
Grossberg and Peterson were charged last month with killing the new-born baby on Nov. 21 last year by disposing of it in a trash container behind a Newark, Delaware, motel after they delivered it.
According to a preliminary report by the state medical examiner, the infant was alive when born and then fatally injured by being shaken and receiving a blow to the head.

At a court hearing last month, defence attorneys indicated their experts believed the infant would not have survived its own congenital deformities or the medical problems suffered by Grossberg early in her pregnancy.
